bands.criteria: Describe visible overall imbalance without inferring diagnoses, disability, or universal unattractiveness.
Multiple visible feature relationships limit overall harmony within this subjective rubric.
Noticeable imbalances in facial proportions or feature relationships; explain the visible observations.
The average reference is 4. Broadly balanced, ordinary facial relationships without pronounced overall strengths or limitations.
Good overall balance and facial harmony; striking features are not necessary.
Good facial harmony and cohesive features, with some visible limitations or less exceptional relationships.
Strong overall harmony and multiple well-integrated features that support an assessment above the attractive anchor.
Very strong facial harmony and cohesive structure; minor limitations may remain without dominating the whole face.
Consistently strong visible feature relationships and exceptional overall harmony; do not require literal flawlessness.
Exceptional whole-face harmony, balance and visible symmetry with distinctive, well-integrated features across assessable regions.
The highest reference band demands unusually compelling visible evidence across the whole face. Eight is a theoretical reference endpoint, not a claim of human perfection.
